items.title: Alexandar Pavlov and Ayiko Solomon, Peace For All Canada
notes:
A. Pavlov and A. Solomo presented on behalf of Peace for All Canada to discuss the current issues related to accessing justice. A copy of their presentation was attached to the agenda. They highlighted that many residents deterred by complexity and cost of legal system and that there is a lack of access to trusted culturally responsive legal supports. They further highlighted that many individuals become involved with the justice system due to unaddressed societal issues such as housing and family supports. They asked that Council support their new initiative, the Community Legal Information Project (CLIP), that will be launching in September of 2025. CLIP will endeavour to provide access to legal information and legal supports such as legal aid and pro bono lawyers. 

Responding to questions, A. Pavlov provided statistics related to the high volume of unrepresented and underrepresented individuals in Ontario courts due to a lack of access to representation, a lack of understanding of the complexities of the justice system, and high legal costs. He also stated that they are partnered with various community organizations such as Supportive Housing Waterloo and Social Development Centre Waterloo Region. A. Solomo confirmed that the Peace for All Canada formed in 2006 and concentrated their assistance typically in eastern Africa, but in 2018 there was a reevaluation that changed their focus to helping the public locally. He explained that they are concentrating on providing supportive services to youth and families. 

In response to the Committee, A. Pavlov explained that the Law Foundation of Ontario has provided six months of funding for the CLIP initiative.

items.title: Andrew Reeves, Kitchener
notes:
A. Reeves spoke on the need for a public camping by-law to legally permit individuals to shelter themselves and have proper access to services such as a bathroom.

In response to Council, A. Reeves suggested that Council look into the City of Hamilton public camping by-law as a model for a similar by-law to be established at the Region as well as collaborate with those with lived experience and local organizations.

notes: K. Regional Chair K. Redman Motion
notes:
J. Erb assumed Chair.

Regional Chair K. Redman provided an overview of her proposed motion. S. Foxton tabled an amendment to the main motion to include the Cambridge Memorial Hospital. 

Wayne Steffler, Commissioner Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, clarified that none of the local hospitals are currently being funded by the Region. He further clarified that in early 2000s there was a funding plan to support special renovation projects at the three hospitals and specifically in 2013 Cambridge Memorial Hospital received $7.8 million. 

C. Huinink stated her opposition to the amending motion as Cambridge Memorial Hospital is a pre-existing hospital, and operational costs are funded by the province not at the Regional level.

In response to Council, K. Redman explained that motion is meant to have the Waterloo Regional Health Network (WHRN) provide information related to the financial implications of a new hospital and to develop a plan in order to move forward with the project. She further explained that this motion is meant to be complimentary to current area municipal staff and Council discussions to ensure community engagement and transparency as the potential project cost may be substantial.

Council discussed the need for potential costs and the overall impact on the taxpayer. 

Regional Chair K. Redman clarified that the Cambridge Memorial Hospital has been involved in these discussions, and she reiterated that the local share is prescribed by the province and the responsibility of the hospital.

S. Foxton expressed support for the motion presented by Regional Chair K. Redman and the amendment is meant to enhance the language to ensure inclusivity of all the hospitals.

1. motions.item_title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee Summary - August 12, 2025
motions.text: WHEREAS ensuring the safety of all road users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers, is a key priority for the Region of Waterloo; AND WHEREAS right turns on red lights can pose significant risks, particularly at major intersections with high volumes of traffic and documented collision histories; AND WHEREAS 89% of pedestrian collisions occur at signalized intersections, 56% of pedestrians struck by vehicles had the right of way, and 1 in 3 pedestrian collisions are caused by a turning vehicle; AND WHEREAS 74% of cycling collisions occur at intersections; AND WHEREAS intersections along regional arterial roads have experienced a number of vehicle and pedestrian-related incidents; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to report back on the feasibility, potential financial impacts, and implementation considerations of: Prohibiting right turns on red at key intersections along regional arterial roads with a documented history of high collision rates involving vehicles and/or pedestrians; and Introducing advanced pedestrian crossing signals (such as Leading Pedestrian Intervals) at those same intersections, which would allow pedestrians to begin crossing before vehicles receive a green light or turn signal; AND THAT the report include an analysis of collision data, potential safety benefits, impacts on traffic flow, operational and infrastructure considerations, consultation with area municipalities, and any best practices from comparable municipalities; AND THAT staff identify and include a preliminary list of possible candidate intersections for potential pilot implementation or further study of these safety measures.
motions.text_html:
1. WHEREAS ensuring the safety of all road users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers, is a key priority for the Region of Waterloo;
    AND WHEREAS right turns on red lights can pose significant risks, particularly at major intersections with high volumes of traffic and documented collision histories;
    AND WHEREAS 89% of pedestrian collisions occur at signalized intersections, 56% of pedestrians struck by vehicles had the right of way, and 1 in 3 pedestrian collisions are caused by a turning vehicle;
    AND WHEREAS 74% of cycling collisions occur at intersections;
    AND WHEREAS intersections along regional arterial roads have experienced a number of vehicle and pedestrian-related incidents;
    THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to report back on the feasibility, potential financial impacts, and implementation considerations of:
    Prohibiting right turns on red at key intersections along regional arterial roads with a documented history of high collision rates involving vehicles and/or pedestrians; and
    Introducing advanced pedestrian crossing signals (such as Leading Pedestrian Intervals) at those same intersections, which would allow pedestrians to begin crossing before vehicles receive a green light or turn signal;
    AND THAT the report include an analysis of collision data, potential safety benefits, impacts on traffic flow, operational and infrastructure considerations, consultation with area municipalities, and any best practices from comparable municipalities;
    AND THAT staff identify and include a preliminary list of possible candidate intersections for potential pilot implementation or further study of these safety measures.

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee Summary - August 12, 2025
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: 1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct staff to: Enter into an agreement with the Township of Woolwich, without prejudice to future cost-sharing agreements, to fund up to $956,000 of the proposed culvert over the Randall Drain at Fountain Street, estimated at $1,533,317, Enter into an agreement with the Township of Woolwich to fund $510,000 toward 50% of the design costs of the proposed sanitary trunk and watermain extending from Kossuth Road along Fountain Street through Jetliner Court to Menno Street, Consider these contributions in lieu of local development charges for airside development at the airport and in lieu of connection charges for current airport operations accessing the sanitary trunk; as outlined in report PDL-GDS-25-010, dated August 12, 2025. 2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo authorize staff to use debentures up to a 30-year term for large-scale growth-related projects that have a longer life and future revenue cycle in future capital budgets as outlined in report COR-TRY-25-022, dated August 12, 2025. 3. WHEREAS democracy is healthy when everyone is able to participate fully and safely and contribute to the well-being of their community; AND WHEREAS we are witnessing the dissolution of democratic discourse and respectful debate across all levels of government and in neighbouring jurisdictions; AND WHEREAS Ontario’s municipally elected officials are dealing with increasingly hostile, unsafe environments facing threats, violence and harassment; AND WHEREAS social media platforms have exacerbated disrespectful dialogue, negative commentary, and toxic engagement which disincentivizes individuals, especially women and candidates from varying backgrounds from running for office; AND WHEREAS better decisions are made when democracy is respectful and constructive and the voices of diverse genders, identities, ethnicities, races, ages and abilities are heard and represented around municipal council tables; AND WHEREAS there are reports and data indicating an increase in harassment and intimidation incidents targeting politicians; AND WHEREAS the Association of Municipalities of Ontario’s Healthy Democracy Project has identified concerning trends with fewer people voting in local elections and running for municipal office; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED: THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo council affirms that a healthy democracy requires the full, safe, and respectful participation of all individuals, and that hostility, harassment, and violence directed toward elected officials, candidates, and community members are direct threats to democratic integrity; AND THAT the Region of Waterloo Council formally endorses and adopts the Elect Respect pledge and commits to advancing a culture of civic engagement rooted in respect, and accountability by: • Modeling respect and integrity in all interactions, public, private, and online; • Actively rejecting and denouncing all forms of abuse, harassment, hate, intimidation, and violence; • Upholding constructive discourse by debating ideas and policies rather than engaging in personal attacks; • Creating inclusive and supportive conditions that encourage and protect the participation of individuals from all genders, identities, races, ethnicities, ages, abilities, and backgrounds in local democracy; • Advocating for robust protections and appropriate responses from law enforcement and governing bodies when threats or harassment occur against elected officials or candidates; and • Holding ourselves and each other accountable to the highest standards of ethical leadership and respectful governance. AND THAT the Region of Waterloo Council calls upon all elected officials, community organizations, and institutions, to endorse and promote the Elect Respect campaign; AND THAT this resolution be forwarded to the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, Ontario’s Big City Mayors, the Federation of Canadian Municipalities, area MPs and MPPs, Waterloo Regional Police Service, Ontario Provincial Police, Wellington County municipalities, and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police to urge coordinated and sustained action in defending democratic engagement and the safety of elected officials. August 12, 2025

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee Summary - August 12, 2025
motions.text: 4. Whereas municipalities across Ontario are increasingly adopting Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) programs as a proven tool to improve road safety, particularly in school zones and community safety zones; Whereas reducing vehicle speeds helps creates calmer, safer neighbourhoods that encourage people to use active forms of transportation and to be active in their communities; Whereas the Region of Waterloo has operated an ASE program since 2021 in partnership with local area municipalities, working closely with the Ontario Traffic Council to adopt and promote best practices; Whereas the Region of Waterloo’s Strategic Plan “Growing with Care” highlights Climate Aligned Growth, calling for the development of complete streets and expanded alternative transportation networks that reduce reliance on cars. The Plan also emphasizes Equitable Services and Opportunities by prioritizing inclusive, accessible services that support community health, safety, and complete communities. The ASE program directly supports these goals by calming traffic, protecting vulnerable road users, and enabling active transportation; Whereas the current legislative and regulatory framework, enabled by the Highway Traffic Act, allows municipalities to operate ASE programs and to independently determine key elements of program delivery; Whereas the Region continues to hear from the community both the need for stronger traffic calming in neighbourhoods and the need for transparency and clarity around ASE program operations; Whereas some municipalities across Ontario have implemented ASE programs with varying approaches, which presents an opportunity to promote consistency and alignment with emerging best practices province-wide; Whereas a program review of ASE operations could increase transparency, public understanding, and trust, and better support the program’s intended outcomes of road safety and speed reduction; Whereas the Government of Ontario passed Bill 34 (Transportation for the Future Act, 2024) on June 5, 2025, introducing new provisions under the Highway Traffic Act (Part XIV.5 – Automated Camera Enforcement for Road Safety), which emphasize transparency and enable new ministerial powers regarding ASE and Red Light Camera programs, with regulations expected in Fall 2025; Therefore be it resolved that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo respectfully request the Province of Ontario, through the Ministry of Transportation to continue to work collaboratively with municipalities that operate ASE programs to: Review and enhance existing regulated signage requirements to improve clarity and understanding for motorists; Establish public reporting requirements that would both enhance public understanding and increase program integrity; Engage with municipalities, road safety experts, law enforcement and adjudication professionals to review the program, including the Highway Traffic Act and relevant regulations to ensure the standards reflect local safety needs while providing province-wide consistency; Provide guidance and tools to support municipalities in standardizing operations with best practices and in enhancing public education around ASE operations; Introduce regulatory requirements to ensure that revenues generated from ASE programs are directed toward local road safety initiatives. And that a copy of this resolution be forwarded to the Minister of Transportation, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), all Ontario municipalities with ASE programs, local MPPs, and the Ontario Traffic Council.
motions.text_html:
4.    Whereas municipalities across Ontario are increasingly adopting Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) programs as a proven tool to improve road safety, particularly in school zones and community safety zones;
Whereas reducing vehicle speeds helps creates calmer, safer neighbourhoods that encourage people to use active forms of transportation and to be active in their communities;
Whereas the Region of Waterloo has operated an ASE program since 2021 in partnership with local area municipalities, working closely with the Ontario Traffic Council to adopt and promote best practices;
Whereas the Region of Waterloo’s Strategic Plan “Growing with Care” highlights Climate Aligned Growth, calling for the development of complete streets and expanded alternative transportation networks that reduce reliance on cars. The Plan also emphasizes Equitable Services and Opportunities by prioritizing inclusive, accessible services that support community health, safety, and complete communities. The ASE program directly supports these goals by calming traffic, protecting vulnerable road users, and enabling active transportation;
Whereas the current legislative and regulatory framework, enabled by the Highway Traffic Act, allows municipalities to operate ASE programs and to independently determine key elements of program delivery;
Whereas the Region continues to hear from the community both the need for stronger traffic calming in neighbourhoods and the need for transparency and clarity around ASE program operations;
Whereas some municipalities across Ontario have implemented ASE programs with varying approaches, which presents an opportunity to promote consistency and alignment with emerging best practices province-wide;
Whereas a program review of ASE operations could increase transparency, public understanding, and trust, and better support the program’s intended outcomes of road safety and speed reduction;
Whereas the Government of Ontario passed Bill 34 (Transportation for the Future Act, 2024) on June 5, 2025, introducing new provisions under the Highway Traffic Act (Part XIV.5 – Automated Camera Enforcement for Road Safety), which emphasize transparency and enable new ministerial powers regarding ASE and Red Light Camera programs, with regulations expected in Fall 2025;
Therefore be it resolved that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo respectfully request the Province of Ontario, through the Ministry of Transportation to continue to work collaboratively with municipalities that operate ASE programs to:

  1. Review and enhance existing regulated signage requirements to improve clarity and understanding for motorists;
  2. Establish public reporting requirements that would both enhance public understanding and increase program integrity;
  3. Engage with municipalities, road safety experts, law enforcement and adjudication professionals to review the program, including the Highway Traffic Act and relevant regulations to ensure the standards reflect local safety needs while providing province-wide consistency;
  4. Provide guidance and tools to support municipalities in standardizing operations with best practices and in enhancing public education around ASE operations;
  5. Introduce regulatory requirements to ensure that revenues generated from ASE programs are directed toward local road safety initiatives.
    And that a copy of this resolution be forwarded to the Minister of Transportation, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), all Ontario municipalities with ASE programs, local MPPs, and the Ontario Traffic Council.

motions.item_title: Community and Health Services Committee Summary - August 12, 2025
motions.text: The Community and Health Services Committee recommends as follows: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action as set out in report CSD-CHS-25-003 dated August 12, 2025: That the Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer be authorized to issue up to $4.4M of debentures to invest in purchasing up to two 88 space modular child care centres to be repaid with a nominal return on investment through a long-term affordable lease rate with not-for-profit child care operators. That the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services be authorized to enter into affordable lease agreements with not-for-profit child care operators identified through an application process supported by Procurement, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor; and That the Commissioner of Community Services be authorized to execute a lease agreement with Waterloo Region District School Board to prepare the land for modular child care, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
The Community and Health Services Committee recommends as follows:

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action as set out in report CSD-CHS-25-003 dated August 12, 2025:
    1. That the Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer be authorized to issue up to $4.4M of debentures to invest in purchasing up to two 88 space modular child care centres to be repaid with a nominal return on investment through a long-term affordable lease rate with not-for-profit child care operators.
    2. That the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services be authorized to enter into affordable lease agreements with not-for-profit child care operators identified through an application process supported by Procurement, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor; and
    3. That the Commissioner of Community Services be authorized to execute a lease agreement with Waterloo Region District School Board to prepare the land for modular child care, with terms and conditions satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.

motions.item_title: Regional Chair K. Redman Motion
motions.text: WHEREAS Waterloo Region is quickly growing to a community of one-million people; WHEREAS the Waterloo Region Health Network (WRHN) is working with all partners to establish a new acute care hospital situated at Bearinger Drive in the City of Waterloo and; WHEREAS Region of Waterloo Council is working diligently to balance the critical needs of our growing community and future affordability; WHEREAS The Local Share Plan, public engagement framework, and the impacts of the hospital on Regional services have yet to be identified with the WRHN; THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED THAT staff work with WRHN and report back on the impacts of the new hospital on the region, and inform on lifecycle benefits and costs to the Region, including impacts on key services such as paramedics, public health, transit and water THAT staff develop a funding and contribution policy framework to guide Regional Council’s decision-making process for the funding of the new hospital and future requests for hospital expansions THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present its initial Local Share Plan and overall Total Project Costs to Regional Council as soon as possible, and THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present a community-wide engagement plan to Region of Waterloo Council as the process of building a new hospital in Waterloo Region advances.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS Waterloo Region is quickly growing to a community of one-million people;

WHEREAS the Waterloo Region Health Network (WRHN) is working with all partners to establish a new acute care hospital situated at Bearinger Drive in the City of Waterloo and;

WHEREAS Region of Waterloo Council is working diligently to balance the critical needs of our growing community and future affordability;

WHEREAS The Local Share Plan, public engagement framework, and the impacts of the hospital on Regional services have yet to be identified with the WRHN;

THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED

THAT staff work with WRHN and report back on the impacts of the new hospital on the region, and inform on lifecycle benefits and costs to the Region, including impacts on key services such as paramedics, public health, transit and water

THAT staff develop a funding and contribution policy framework to guide Regional Council’s decision-making process for the funding of the new hospital and future requests for hospital expansions

THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present its initial Local Share Plan and overall Total Project Costs to Regional Council as soon as possible, and

THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present a community-wide engagement plan to Region of Waterloo Council as the process of building a new hospital in Waterloo Region advances.

motions.item_title: Regional Chair K. Redman Motion
motions.text: AMENDMENT WHEREAS Waterloo Region is quickly growing to a community of one-million people; WHEREAS the Waterloo Region Health Network (WRHN) is working with all partners to establish a new acute care hospital situated at Bearinger Drive in the City of Waterloo in combination with the renewal and expansion of existing facilities situated within the City of Kitchener and; WHEREAS Cambridge Memorial Hospital will also have future expansion projects to support the additional health care demands attributed to growth; WHEREAS Region of Waterloo Council is working diligently to balance the critical needs of our growing community and future affordability; WHEREAS The Local Share Plan, public engagement framework, and the impacts of the two hospitals on Regional services have yet to be identified with the WRHN or future requirements associated with Cambridge Memorial Hospital; THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED THAT staff work with WRHN and Cambridge Memorial Hospital and report back on the impacts of the new hospital and the future expansion at Cambridge Memorial Hospital on the region, and inform on lifecycle benefits and costs to the Region, including impacts on key services such as paramedics, public health, transit and water; THAT staff develop a funding and contribution policy framework to guide Regional Council's decision-making process for the funding of the new WRHN hospital and rehabilitation / expansion of existing facilities and, future requests for hospital expansions proposed for Cambridge Memorial Hospital; THAT Cambridge Memorial Hospital and the WRHN be encouraged to work together to develop and articulate the framework in support of a Local Share Plan to facilitate the renewal and rehabilitation of existing facilities and, the establishment of the new hospital for the time period through to 2041; THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present its initial Local Share Plan and overall Total Project Costs to Regional Council as soon as possible, and THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present a community-wide engagement plan to Region of Waterloo Council as the process of building a new hospital in Waterloo Region advances.
motions.text_html:
AMENDMENT

WHEREAS Waterloo Region is quickly growing to a community of one-million people;

WHEREAS the Waterloo Region Health Network (WRHN) is working with all partners to establish a new acute care hospital situated at Bearinger Drive in the City of Waterloo in combination with the renewal and expansion of existing facilities situated within the City of Kitchener and;

WHEREAS Cambridge Memorial Hospital will also have future expansion projects to support the additional health care demands attributed to growth;

WHEREAS Region of Waterloo Council is working diligently to balance the critical needs of our growing community and future affordability;

WHEREAS The Local Share Plan, public engagement framework, and the impacts of the two hospitals on Regional services have yet to be identified with the WRHN or future requirements associated with Cambridge Memorial Hospital;

THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED

THAT staff work with WRHN and Cambridge Memorial Hospital and report back on the impacts of the new hospital and the future expansion at Cambridge Memorial Hospital on the region, and inform on lifecycle benefits and costs to the Region, including impacts on key services such as paramedics, public health, transit and water;

THAT staff develop a funding and contribution policy framework to guide Regional Council's decision-making process for the funding of the new WRHN hospital and rehabilitation / expansion of existing facilities and, future requests for hospital expansions proposed for Cambridge Memorial Hospital;

THAT Cambridge Memorial Hospital and the WRHN be encouraged to work together to develop and articulate the framework in support of a Local Share Plan to facilitate the renewal and rehabilitation of existing facilities and, the establishment of the new hospital for the time period through to 2041;

THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present its initial Local Share Plan and overall Total Project Costs to Regional Council as soon as possible, and

THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present a community-wide engagement plan to Region of Waterloo Council as the process of building a new hospital in Waterloo Region advances.
